new_statements.quote: The final syllable of a word receives stress. There is no evidence of phonemic stress.
new_statements.citation: Wikipedia contributors, 'Tabar language', English Wikipedia, rev. 1330604573 (last edited 1 Jan 2026), section Phonology > Stress, reporting Hong, Steven & Holly Hong. 2003. Grammar Essentials of the Mandara Language of New Ireland Province, ms., SIL PNG, p. 9

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the last syllable of the word; stress is not contrastive (as reported by Wikipedia from Hong & Hong 2003: 9).
new_statements.exceptions: None reported in the second-hand summary.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('the final syllable of a word'); the Wikipedia phonology paragraph states it describes the Simberi-Northern Tatau dialect of Mandara. Second-hand: the primary (Hong & Hong 2003: 9) could not be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: Mandara = Tabar [tbf], Tabar Islands, New Ireland (not the Chadic Mandara/Wandala). The reported stress statement describes the Simberi-Northern Tatau dialect (Mandara dialects: Simberi, Tatau, Tabar); no separate Glottolog dialect code seen in the languoid record.

sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Tabar appears ~95 times (PNI reconstructions, ch. 8 sound correspondences, grammatical examples 4.8, 4.23); the eight stress passages in the book concern Ali/Schouten and tone notation, none about Tabar. No Tabar stress statement.

sources.citation: Beaumont, C. H. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 387-397.
sources.note: Classification and sound-correspondence notes; Tabar mentioned six times (cognate percentages, reflexes of *v, *r); no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Beaumont, Clive H. 1972. New Ireland languages: a review. Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-35), 1-41.
sources.note: Section 1.4 Phonology (pp. 21-22) is a survey of consonants/vowels/tone across New Ireland languages; for Tabar it only reports 'ts'; the only stress remark concerns Tigak (Beaumont 1969 'conclusions on stress need revision'); 1.4.9 notes tone in Kara and Barok. Nothing on Tabar stress.
